name: blast-hole-picking-visual
description: Redesign P4/#21: drill holes join the P2 scene-picking system. Clicking a hole marker shows a selection ring plus the bottom selection bar with the hole's id, depth, and a Focus action; Esc deselects both. #553: a hole ordered by drill_plan grid sits as an undrilled ghost (plannedDrillHoles) until its own drill_hole action completes — this scenario confirms the plan, then ticks until the single hole actually lands (drillHoles) before clicking it, exercising the real, drilled marker the click-selection system targets.

steps.description: Setup: a fresh, staffed site with open ground around the origin — a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, hired/purchased for free (#551), exactly what #553's automatic drill dispatch needs.

steps.command: drill_plan grid origin:10,10 rows:1 cols:1 spacing:3 depth:6
steps.description: Setup: a single drill hole (H1) at a known position — its own position is the click target. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. #553: confirming the grid queues one drill_hole PendingAction and orders H1 (plannedDrillHoles) — it is not drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 here.

expect.note: H1 is ordered (ghost) — not yet drilled (#553).

steps.description: #553: let the staffed driller/drill_rig actually walk to, board, drive to, and drill H1. Mid/end-of-drilling screenshot for the visual channel — the single hole should now render as a real, drilled marker rather than a ghost. Tick count is a first estimate from the spec's duration formula and staffed spawn offsets — tune once real timing is observed running against the implementation.

expect.note: H1 has landed in drillHoles — the click-selection steps below target this real, drilled hole.

steps.description: Click the hole marker — a dashed selection ring appears on the ground and the bottom selection bar shows the hole's id/depth and a Focus action

expect.note: waitForSelector above only proved the button exists; usable proves it is genuinely clickable

steps.description: Esc deselects — the ring and the selection bar both disappear

expect.note: Esc hides the selection bar entirely, same invariant as scene-picking-visual.json's building Esc-deselect check
